payload.claim: `Agent.event` was previously unreachable (always `None`, per the spec's own problem statement); this migration is what actually starts writing the full, untruncated parsed cell-event dict to `events.jsonl` on every turn. Before this change, only `_describe`'s bounded renderings ever reached persistence (e.g. `tool_result` became the fixed string "agent: tool ok/error", `text` and `tool_use` were truncated to 160/120 chars before being handed to `watch`). Now the raw dict — which for `text`/`tool_use`/`tool_result` events can carry full file contents, command output, or anything the untrusted cell chose to emit on stdout — is persisted verbatim to a host-side control-plane artifact that the `secrets` gate never scans (it only reads the diff). Nothing in this spec's scope or tests addresses whether `events.jsonl` should be size-capped or secret-scanned now that it actually carries this content; the golden-fixture and unit tests only ever exercise small synthetic dicts, so the volume/sensitivity change is invisible to the suite.
